clue.text: Miss a celebration

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman, informally a gal

explanation.surface: Someone skips a party they were invited to.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or special celebratory event.

clue.text: Stand by setter's final composition

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it, to abide it
by in the sense of alongside or together with
the setter refers to themself as me; the possessive is no extra letter

explanation.surface: Loyally supporting the crossword compiler through their last piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' is the FA Cup Final, at which this hymn is traditionally sung before kick-off; the FA Cup is English football's knockout competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The hymn is sung by the crowd at every FA Cup Final, so it is the Final's own piece of music.

clue.text: Heathen is cheat, it turns out

indicators.note: how things turn out is how they end up arranged, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that an unbeliever is also a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathen as an adjective describes one without religious belief, the godless outlook of an unbeliever.

clue.text: With both sides' agreement, separate savings account to be dumped?

indicators.note: read with dumped, these words say the pieces are to be put into the bin, so they go inside it

parts.note: something dumped is binned, thrown in the bin
to separate is to part
an ISA is a British tax-free savings account, an Individual Savings Account

explanation.surface: A couple splitting up agree to close their joint savings account.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'to be dumped' means 'to go in the BIN'. An ISA is the UK's Individual Savings Account.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipartisan measure has the agreement of both opposing parties or sides.

clue.text: Scrap round hairdo — it's boring

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a scrap is a fight, a brawl
a DA (duck's arse) is a 1950s greased-back hairstyle

explanation.surface: Someone finds a fight over a haircut tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'dull' but means 'making holes'. The DA, a quiff swept back to a point at the nape, is an old slang hairstyle name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small pointed hand tool used to bore holes in wood.

clue.text: Kid to make member of relay team redundant?

definitions.meaning: to kid is to tease or fool someone playfully

definitions.text: to make member of relay team redundant?
definitions.meaning: each runner in a relay runs one leg, so taking away a runner's leg is drawing it off the team

explanation.surface: Teasing a teammate by dropping them from the relay squad.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to tease or fool someone with a joke, which is what kidding them is.

clue.text: School over, soak and shower

parts.note: to ret flax or hemp is to soak it to soften the fibres
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: After lessons finish, the children get drenched in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' is the less familiar RET, the soaking of flax.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone again, to teach them over, is to retrain them.

clue.text: Reserve catching cold needs a breather

indicators.note: the reserve catches, holds, the cold letter within it

parts.note: a reserve player is a substitute, a sub
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A substitute player who has caught a chill needs a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest but means a device for breathing underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuba gear is breathing apparatus for divers, so it is literally a breather.

clue.text: Jogger may start to go naked?

indicators.note: to read as put to, against and into, so the go letter joins the inside of the naked piece

parts.note: naked means nude

indicators.note: the start of the word go is its first letter

explanation.surface: A runner might begin to run without any clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a loose container signal, helped by the question mark: G, the start of 'go', is put into NUDE. 'Jogger' is not a runner but something that jogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a little push that jogs someone, so it is a jogger of the memory or elbow.

clue.text: School volunteers I fired scarper

parts.note: a high is short for high school
the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: Pupils and part-time soldiers flee after someone opens fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To hightail it is American slang for running away fast, as to scarper is in British slang.

clue.text: Finance sport with old money

parts.note: sport in the sense of fun or amusement
d was the abbreviation for the old British penny, before 1971 decimalisation

explanation.surface: Paying for a game using pre-decimal coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old money' is D, the pre-1971 British penny (from Latin denarius).
explanation.definitionFit: To finance something is to fund it, providing the money it needs.

clue.text: Viewer's part to keep article going to the end

indicators.note: the article letter travels from its place to the end of the word

parts.note: to keep is to retain
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to a newspaper piece until they finish reading it.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer of the eye, part of the organ that does the viewing.

clue.text: Satisfy grasping, ghastly dance acts

indicators.note: one piece holds, grasps, the other inside it

parts.note: to slake a thirst is to satisfy it
ghastly in the sense of deathly pale, wan

explanation.surface: A critic finds terrible dance performances fulfil every expectation of awfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballet is a danced work in four acts, so it is a set of dance acts.

clue.text: Source of ruination to plant?

parts.note: the mafia's farewell kiss marks someone for killing, as an informer or plant planted in the gang would receive, and it also means anything that dooms an enterprise

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an action that ensures something's ruin, from the kiss signalling a mafia execution.

clue.text: Punch dispenser initially runs out

indicators.note: the letter for runs goes out, leaving the word

parts.note: initially means at first, first
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A drinks machine's supply of fruit punch is the first thing to run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch dispenser' suggests a bar, but a fist dispenses punches.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand is what delivers a blow, so it dispenses punches.

clue.text: Girl keeps back right adornment for garden plant

indicators.note: the girl keeps, holds, the other letters inside her

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: back means the right and adornment pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: a garden gnome is a little ornamental figure

explanation.surface: A girl holds on to a rear decoration suited to a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns R and GNOME together, making EMONGR, which LASS holds: L-EMONGR-ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemongrass is a tropical grass grown for its lemon-scented stems, a culinary plant.

clue.text: They're resting on mobile

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so these letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Things sitting on top of a mobile phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringtones are the call sounds stored on a mobile phone, sitting there until a call comes.

clue.text: During cut in coke supply, hard to bottle it

indicators.note: the hard letter goes during, within, the other letters
supply read as an adverb, supplely, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Dealers chicken out when cocaine supplies are cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the adverb of supple (flexibly), anagramming CUTINCOKE; 'During' puts H inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle it is British slang for losing your nerve, the same as backing out through fear.

clue.text: One flying from African province 'into Eastern home counties

indicators.note: the province goes into, inside, the other letters

parts.note: the home counties, those around London, are in the SE, the south-east of England
the Cape Province was a province of South Africa

explanation.surface: Someone flies in from South Africa to the counties east of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the English counties surrounding London, hence SE for south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapee is one who flees, flying from captivity.

clue.text: Radio's administrative body with restrictions on members

indicators.note: what is broadcast on radio is heard, not read, so the sound counts

parts.note: a trust is a body administering property or an institution

explanation.surface: A broadcasting organisation imposes limits on its membership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' are limbs, not people in an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means tied up, with arms and legs bound, so the limbs are restricted.

clue.text: Turn on green light in corner

indicators.note: turn means the following little word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: giving the green light is giving the OK

explanation.surface: Flicking on a green lamp in a dark corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or corner of a room.

clue.text: Nothing stops doctor touching pedestrian

indicators.note: nothing stops up, plugs, the doctor

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
O is nought, nothing
re means concerning, touching on

explanation.surface: Nothing prevents a doctor from striking a person on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' is the adjective meaning dull, not a person walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and ordinary, just about average quality.

clue.text: Starts off mare's colt, jumping over big rotten post

indicators.note: the starts of each of these words are taken

explanation.surface: A mare's young foal leaps over a big decaying fence post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' means a job, not a fence post.
explanation.definitionFit: A McJob is a low-paid, dead-end job with no prospects, a poor post.

clue.text: Duke has superior way of passing port

parts.note: going over is passing above, the superior route

explanation.surface: A nobleman takes the high road on his way through a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the Channel port in Kent, south-east England.

clue.text: DIY nut relocated missing order

indicators.note: relocated means moved to new places, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A home-improvement enthusiast moves house and loses track of what they ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' means enthusiast, here a fan of do-it-yourself home improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy means lacking neatness, without order.

clue.text: I have to judge dance

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone is called on to judge a dance contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive is a lively jazz and swing dance.

clue.text: Ice cream, we hear, on hand for a feast

indicators.note: on means placed after, the sundae piece follows the hand

parts.note: the palm is the inside of the hand

indicators.note: what we hear is heard spoken, so the sound counts, not spelling

parts.note: a sundae is an ice cream dessert

explanation.surface: An ice-cream treat held in the hand for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday before Easter is a Christian feast day commemorating Christ's entry into Jerusalem.

clue.text: Assorted real plugs asked for with exposed pins

indicators.note: the jumbled letters plug, fill a gap in, the other piece

parts.note: begged means asked for

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Various electric plugs requested that have bare pins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pins' is slang for legs. Assorted REAL gives AREL, which plugs BEGGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pins is informal for legs, so having them exposed is having bare legs.

clue.text: Smoke's part sulphur, and other gases

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
O and H are the chemical symbols for oxygen and hydrogen, two gases

explanation.surface: A chemist describes smoke's makeup: sulphur and other gases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is British slang for London, of which this district is a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London's West End, a part of the city nicknamed the Smoke.
